definitions.explanation: Physical movement of one's body. Most commonly used in the negative form to describe being unable to move due to being trapped, crowded, or otherwise constrained.

examples.japanese: {身動|みうご}きが{取|と}れない。
{満員|まんいん}{電車|でんしゃ}で{身動|みうご}きが{取|と}れなかった。
examples.english: I couldn't move on the packed train.

examples.japanese: {借金|しゃっきん}が{増|ふ}えすぎて、{経済的|けいざいてき}に{身動|みうご}きが{取|と}れない{状態|じょうたい}になってしまった。
examples.english: The debt piled up so much that I ended up in a situation where I couldn't move financially.

notes:
USAGE: {身動|みうご}き is almost always used in the negative pattern {身動|みうご}きが{取|と}れない (unable to move). It can describe physical inability to move (in a crowd, when restrained) or figurative inability to act (due to financial problems, obligations, etc.).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {身動|みうご}きが{取|と}れない: unable to move, stuck
- {身動|みうご}きできない: unable to stir
- {身動|みうご}き{一|ひと}つしない: not moving a muscle

The word is a compound of {身|み} (body) and {動|うご}き (movement).
